name: fabric
line: Bass you feel through your feet before your ears.
note: Three rooms that genuinely differ, which is the whole point — Room 1 is the heavy one and the floor physically vibrates, Room 2 is the warmer house room with the best booth, Room 3 is where the risks get taken. Sunday morning closes are the real fabric.

rooms.name: Room 1
rooms.note: Bodysonic floor. Techno, DnB, jungle. Loud enough to be a physical event.

rooms.name: Room 2
rooms.note: House, disco, garage. Warmer, more human, better for a set with dynamics.

rooms.name: Room 3
rooms.note: Leftfield and newer bookings. Small, gets sweaty fast.

name: Corsica Studios
line: Two dark boxes under a railway arch, booked with taste.
note: The room most London DJs name when asked where they'd rather play. Small, dark, no VIP nonsense, and the programming has been consistently ahead for fifteen years. If you only have one night, this is the safest bet for quality over spectacle.

rooms.name: Room 1
rooms.note: The main box. Low ceiling, heavy low end.

rooms.name: Room 2
rooms.note: Smaller, weirder, often the better room.

nights: Programming is promoter-led — check listings rather than the day

name: FOLD
line: Industrial, relentless, no phones, no daylight.
note: The closest London gets to a Berlin room. Strict no-photo policy that is actually enforced, which changes the floor completely. Come for the long haul or don't come — arriving at midnight and leaving at 3 misses the entire idea.

rooms.name: Room 1
rooms.note: The main industrial room. Hard, fast, dark.

nights: Weekend-long events — Fri night through Sunday

name: Phonox
line: One DJ, all night, every Saturday for months.
note: Built around the residency model — a single artist takes every Saturday for a season, which means the room and the crowd actually develop a relationship. Best value night out in London if the resident suits you.

name: XOYO
line: Big names on a 13-week residency, central and easy.
note: The residency programme is the draw — you get a headliner curating three months rather than a one-off. Central enough that it's an easy add-on, commercial enough that the crowd varies a lot by night.
nights: 13-week residencies — check who is holding the season

name: Village Underground
line: Victorian warehouse, high ceilings, tube carriages on the roof.
note: A big single room with real architecture — brick arches and proper height, which makes it feel like an event rather than a basement. Doubles as a live venue, so the booking swings between gigs and club nights.
nights: Promoter-led — mix of live shows and club nights

name: Drumsheds
line: A decommissioned IKEA the size of an airfield.
note: Four enormous halls in an ex-IKEA. It is a festival site with a roof, so expect festival trade-offs — long queues, big crowds, a long trip north. Worth it for the lineups you can't see anywhere else in the city.

rooms.name: Halls x4
rooms.note: Each hall is programmed separately — check which one your artist is in before committing to a walk.

nights: Large one-off events, often daytime into night

name: Venue MOT Unit 18
line: A shed by the railway with better sound than most clubs.
note: Raw in the way that matters. No decor budget, all of it spent on the rig and the bookings. The most exciting room in London for anything leftfield, dub-adjacent or genuinely underground.

name: Colour Factory
line: Hackney Wick warehouse, canal outside, sound-first.
note: One of the better-sounding mid-size rooms in the east. Canalside, so summer daytime events spill outside. Programming leans house, breaks and UK bass.
nights: Weekend club nights, occasional day parties

name: E1
line: Long warehouse, hard programming, east London late.
note: A proper warehouse shape — long and narrow, which makes the room feel packed even when it isn't. Leans harder and faster than most of the city. Adjoining outdoor space in summer.

name: Brilliant Corners
line: Records played properly, at conversation volume, with food.
note: Not a club and doesn't pretend to be. Japanese-style listening bar with a hi-fi worth travelling for — vinyl, no mixing, no dancing. The right place for the night before or the night after, and a genuinely good ear-reset.

name: Ormside Projects
line: Small railway-arch warehouse, hard and unfussy.
note: In the same South Bermondsey cluster as Venue MOT — you can do both in a night. Dark, low, no frills, and a crowd that came for the music.

name: Printworks
line: A newspaper printing hall, 100m long, lit like a film.
note: The Press Halls were the most photographed room in British clubbing — a 100-metre corridor with the printing gantries still overhead. Closed in 2023 for the Canada Water redevelopment with a return announced under Broadwick. VERIFY current status before planning anything around it.

name: Rex Club
line: The best-sounding room in France, and it knows it.
note: Laurent Garnier's home room and the spiritual centre of French techno since the late 80s. The system is the reason to go — you hear things in records here you have never heard. Low ceiling, black walls, no distractions.

name: Djoon
line: Soulful house for people who actually dance.
note: The warm end of Paris. Deep, soulful, disco and Afro-house, and a crowd that dances properly rather than facing the booth. If you want the opposite of a techno night, this is it — and the Sunday sessions are the real thing.

name: Badaboum
line: Small club, cocktail room next door, one of the best booths in Europe.
note: The layout is the trick — a proper dark club room, and through a door, a completely separate cocktail bar with a totally different mood. You can reset and go back in. The booth is famously good and DJs love playing here.

rooms.name: Bar
rooms.note: Separate cocktail room. Talk, reset, go back in.

name: La Station — Gare des Mines
hours: Fri–Sat, often free entry, outdoor yard in summer
line: A disused freight station run like a squat, and better for it.
note: Cheap or free, on the edge of the périphérique, run as a collective. Programming is the most adventurous in Paris — experimental, club, noise, whatever. Outdoor courtyard makes it a great summer daytime option.
nights: Fri–Sat, collective-programmed, often free before midnight

name: La Machine du Moulin Rouge
line: Three floors attached to the Moulin Rouge, oddly enough.
note: Central, big, three levels each with its own character, plus a rooftop bar. Touristy location but the bookings are serious. Good option when you want scale without going to the suburbs.

rooms.name: Le Bar à Bulles
rooms.note: Rooftop terrace. Air and a cigarette.

name: Dehors Brut
hours: Daytime — roughly 14:00 to midnight, summer season
line: Open-air concrete under the Bercy arches, in daylight.
note: The Paris day-party. Runs through the warm months in an open concrete space near Bercy. Different energy entirely — sunglasses, beers, house music, home by midnight.

name: Nuits Fauves
line: Under the bridge by the river, hard and late.
note: Riverside, near the Austerlitz cluster, and harder than most of the city. Terrace on the Seine is a good escape valve. Pairs naturally with Djoon in the same area if you want two moods in one night.

rooms.name: Terrasse
rooms.note: On the Seine. Sunrise here is worth staying for.

name: Glazart
hours: Indoor late; La Plage outdoor daytime in summer
line: An actual sand beach on the edge of the ring road.
note: They trucked in sand and made a beach in a car park by the périphérique, and it works. Free or cheap outdoor sessions all summer. Indoor room runs harder and later the rest of the year.

rooms.name: La Plage
rooms.note: The sand. Summer daytime, often free.

nights: Summer: outdoor daytime. Year-round: indoor weekends.

name: Petit Bain
hours: Evenings into the night, rooftop in summer
line: A floating barge with a rooftop and a garden.
note: A boat moored on the Seine with a restaurant, a rooftop, and a club room in the hull. Lighter programming, great for an early-evening start before something heavier. Rooftop at sunset is the draw.

name: La Java
line: A 1920s dance hall basement in Belleville.
note: Historic room — Piaf played here — now a sweaty basement with good leftfield and club bookings. Belleville location means the night can continue in every direction afterwards.

name: Silencio
hours: Members until midnight, then open to the public
line: David Lynch designed a members' club and it looks like it.
note: Gold-leafed, mirrored, six metres underground, designed by Lynch himself. Members only until midnight, public after — which is the move. Not a rave. Go for the room and a late drink, not for a peak-time set.

name: T7
line: Warehouse techno on the southern edge, no pretence.
note: Out past the périphérique in Ivry — a proper industrial box for hard techno and big lineups. The Paris answer to a Berlin warehouse. Plan the journey home; it's not central.

name: Concrete
line: The boat that invented the Paris after-hours.
note: Closed in 2019. Listed because it changed the city — the Saturday-morning start and the 24-hour licence campaign that followed came out of here, and most of the current Paris scene grew from that crew. RIP.

name: Berghain / Panorama Bar
hours: Saturday midnight through Monday morning. Klubnacht is the main event.
line: Three rooms, three completely different nights, one building.
note: The door is a real filter and there is no formula — dress dark, come in twos, be sober enough to answer a question, don't queue on your phone. Inside: no photos, ever, and the sense of time genuinely disappears. Sunday afternoon in Panorama Bar with the shutters open is the single best hour in European clubbing.

rooms.name: Berghain
rooms.note: The main hall. Steel, concrete, 18m ceiling, unrelenting techno.

rooms.name: Panorama Bar
rooms.note: Upstairs. House, disco, garage. Shutters open Sunday morning and the light comes in.

rooms.name: Säule
rooms.note: Downstairs. Experimental, ambient, drone, leftfield. Where the risks live.

name: Tresor
hours: Wed, Fri, Sat — late into the next day
line: A strobe-lit tunnel in a decommissioned power station.
note: The birthplace of the Berlin–Detroit axis and still the hardest room in the city. The downstairs vault is a long corridor of steel bars and strobes with almost no light — you can't see the DJ, which is the point. Globus upstairs is the warm relief.

rooms.name: Tresor (vault)
rooms.note: The tunnel. Strobes, steel, no visibility. Detroit and Berlin techno.

rooms.name: Globus
rooms.note: Upstairs. House, disco, warmer, better air.

rooms.name: Kraftwerk
rooms.note: The vast turbine hall. Used for concerts, Atonal, large events.

name: ://about blank
hours: Fri and Sat into Monday. Garden opens in daylight.
line: Two floors and a garden you can still be in on Monday.
note: Collectively run, explicitly political, and one of the few big rooms where the politics are on the wall rather than in the marketing. The garden is the reason to stay — trees, sculptures, daylight, and people who arrived on Friday. Zug um Zug and the long-running parties here are institutions.

rooms.name: Garden
rooms.note: Outdoors, daylight, trees. The recovery zone.

nights: Fri and Sat, running into Monday

name: Sisyphos
line: A former dog-biscuit factory that became a permanent festival.
note: Multiple outdoor stages, a lake, a beach, a boat, sculptures, and a party that genuinely does not stop from Friday to Monday. Less about the bookings and more about the site — go in summer, go in daylight, don't plan an exit time.
nights: Friday night through Monday morning, every weekend

name: RSO
line: Industrial hall, fast techno, outdoor area, very loud.
note: One of the newer big rooms and one of the hardest. Raw industrial space with a large outdoor section, programmed for the faster end of contemporary techno. If Berghain's door defeats you, this is a real alternative rather than a consolation.

name: KitKatClub
line: Sex-positive, dress-coded, and the music is genuinely good.
note: The dress code is enforced and it is not a costume party — fetish, latex, or very little. Inside it's relaxed, respectful and much less intimidating than the reputation suggests. Shares a building with Sage; the pool room is real.

name: Club der Visionäre / Hoppetosse
hours: CDV from afternoon; Hoppetosse late and long
line: A wooden shack on a canal, a willow tree, and minimal house until sunrise.
note: The best afternoon in Berlin. A tiny wooden platform on the water where people have been dancing since the afternoon, and a moored boat next door for when it gets late. Minimal, dub-house, deep. Summer only for the outdoor part.

rooms.name: Club der Visionäre
rooms.note: Outdoor, canal-side, from the afternoon. Summer.

rooms.name: Hoppetosse
rooms.note: The boat. Downstairs hull room runs late and long.

nights: CDV daily in summer from afternoon; Hoppetosse weekends late

name: Salon zur Wilden Renate
hours: Fri–Sat into Monday, garden in summer
line: A wrecked apartment building you get lost inside.
note: Three floors of an old apartment block, each room furnished like somebody's flat, plus a garden and a labyrinth. Getting lost is the intended experience. Under long-standing threat from the A100 motorway extension — VERIFY it's still open.

name: OHM
line: The power station's battery room, now the city's best small room.
note: In the old battery room of the Kraftwerk complex, next to Tresor. Tiled, small, and programmed for electro, experimental and the more cerebral end of club music. Where you go when the main room is too obvious.

name: Trauma Bar und Kino
line: Art performance and hard club music in the same night.
note: Where the club and the art world actually overlap — performance, fashion, deconstructed club, and lineups that don't look like anyone else's. Visually the most ambitious room in the city. Not a place to go on autopilot.
nights: Fri–Sat, art and club crossover programming

name: Else
hours: Summer season, afternoon into the night
line: Riverside sand, a dome, and a long summer afternoon.
note: Open-air on the Spree next to the old Eisfabrik site, with a geodesic dome and sand underfoot. Summer season only. The daytime-into-night arc here is one of the best in Berlin.

name: Panke
line: Broken beat, jazz, hip-hop — the non-techno Berlin.
note: A courtyard space in Wedding programming the parts of Black music culture that Berlin's techno monoculture ignores — broken beat, jazz, soul, hip-hop, live bands. Cheap, friendly, and a genuine relief.
nights: Live and DJ programming, most weekends

name: Watergate
line: Floor-to-ceiling windows over the Spree at sunrise.
note: Closed at the end of 2024 after 22 years. The Water Floor's glass wall onto the river, with the sun coming up behind the Oberbaumbrücke, was one of the defining images of Berlin clubbing. RIP.

name: De School
line: The building went. The crew, the ethos and the standard did not.
note: The physical school closed, but the collective and its programming continue through pop-ups and curated takeovers across the city. This is the crew that set the Amsterdam standard — zero phones, pure music, dark room — and that prioritised local resident selectors over guest-name booking. Uncompromising techno and house.
nights: Pop-ups and takeovers — follow the crew, not an address

name: Garage Noord
line: Land a gig here and you have the stamp of cool.
note: An old car repair shop in Amsterdam-Noord, and the absolute hotbed for leftfield and experimental club music, industrial rhythms and fast-tempo sounds. If you are an underground artist and you land a gig here, you have officially earned the ultimate stamp of cool among music lovers.

name: Parallel
line: Paradiso's incubator in the North. Where underground crosses over.
note: Paradiso's sister venue in the North, acting as a dedicated incubator that bridges raw underground talent and mid-sized club spaces. Leans hard into forward-thinking club sounds and global electronic mutations — electronic Amapiano, high-tempo edits, hybrid bass — and serves as the launchpad for acts moving into the mainstream.

name: Radion
line: A former dental clinic running 24 hours on raw concrete.
note: A former dental clinic turned 24-hour cultural sanctuary, highly respected for its raw industrial concrete aesthetic and deep, hypnotic techno bookings. They don't chase radio hits — they book artists who master the art of the extended storytelling set.

name: Paradiso
line: A 19th-century church that is still a rite of passage.
note: A converted 19th-century church that remains a sacred rite of passage. For electronic music lovers its late-night transformations and specialised ADE curations — the STOOR live hardware jams among them — prove it still holds immense cultural capital and respect.

rooms.name: Grote Zaal
rooms.note: The main church hall — balconies, stained glass, the room everyone means.

name: Melkweg
line: A dairy factory big enough to host the niche room and the huge one at once.
note: A historic former dairy factory that has championed electronic music since the dawn of the Dutch rave scene. It hosts massive names, but the multi-room layout lets it run niche, cutting-edge underground nights — drum & bass, specialised techno, UK garage — on the same weekend.

rooms.name: Max
rooms.note: The big hall. Where the massive names land.

rooms.name: Oude Zaal / Rabozaal
rooms.note: The smaller rooms, where the cutting-edge nights run.

name: Lofi
line: A bus garage rebuilt for house and techno purists.
note: A relatively young but massively influential industrial warehouse space in the West, in a repurposed GVB bus garage. It has quickly become a premier destination for house and techno purists — exceptional sound design, extended daytime raves, and community-driven lineups.

name: Shelter
line: Down a hatch into a pitch-black basement. Nothing to look at, by design.
note: Directly underneath the A'DAM Tower, you descend a hatch into a pitch-black concrete basement. World-class Funktion-One, zero visual distractions, no phones. Entirely dedicated to the depths of house and techno, and built specifically for the dancers.

name: NDSM Warehouse
line: A shipbuilding hangar the size of a district. Scale without the sellout.
note: The sprawling industrial docklands venue that hosts festivals like DGTL. Despite the scale it keeps real prestige, because the programming stays fiercely focused on high-concept melodic techno, raw industrial beats and underground legends rather than commercial EDM.

name: AMAZE
line: Eight stages of ID&T spectacle, built for total sensory immersion.
note: A high-tech multi-room audiovisual labyrinth created by ID&T. Futuristic and premium, but it bypasses cheap club tropes by focusing on complete sensory immersion, spatial 11D sound, and booking refined, deep electronic selectors who use the technology to tell a complex sonic story.
